title: Commits and git log
idea: A commit is a saved snapshot of your project with a message. `git log` lists commits, newest first.

analogy.text: Save points in a video game. Each save records the whole game at that moment, and you can reload any earlier one.
analogy.breaks: Git saves only when you commit, and you choose what goes in.

points: `git add` stages changes: it picks what goes into the next commit.
`git commit -m "message"` saves the staged changes as one new commit.
Each commit links to its parent, the commit before it, forming a chain.
`git log` walks that chain from `HEAD`; `--oneline` prints one line per commit.

steps.caption: The first commit, A, has no parent. `main` points at it, and `HEAD` points at `main`.
Commit B records A as its parent. `main` moves forward to B, and `HEAD` follows.
Commit C extends the chain. `git log` starts at `HEAD` and follows parents back to A.

code.title: Three commits
code.caption: Real Git output. Hashes and dates are fixed in this recording; yours will differ.

walk.text: `git add` stages the file. The short status shows `A`: staged as a new file.
Commit with a message. Git prints the branch, a short hash and the message.
A second commit: write the file, stage it, commit it.
A third commit changes the same file. It stores the new version.
One line per commit, newest first. In a terminal, Git also marks `HEAD -> main`.
`-1` shows only the newest commit, in full: hash, author, date, message.

pitfalls: Write messages that say what changed: `Add login route`, not `update`.
`git add .` stages everything here. Run `git status` first, and list private files in `.gitignore`.
Never commit a secret: deleting the file later leaves it in history.

quiz.q: `git show HEAD:f.txt` prints the committed copy. What does it print?
quiz.code:
echo one > f.txt
git add f.txt
echo two > f.txt
git commit -m "Add f"
git show HEAD:f.txt
quiz.why: `git add` stages the file as it is at that moment. The later edit is not staged, so the commit holds `one`.

takeaway: Stage deliberately, commit small, and let `git log` tell the story.
